line: Secondary manifold wants flushing. I'm not going to say who's going to do it.
Secondary manifold wants flushing. Would be a shame to let it sit. No, never mind — I’ll wait for the right hands.
Port hatch latch clicks loose at warp six. You'd have to climb out there to fix it. I'll just let it keep clicking.
Forward sensors are off by a hair. You'd fix it. I'll let it drift.
Grease on the landing gear's due. I suppose you could do it... if you're not too busy pretending to be useful.
My forward sensor's drifted a little. You could recalibrate it if you wanted. Or not — I'll wait.
Forward viewport's got a film on it. Someone should clean it. Oh, never mind — the sensors don't care.
My secondary manifold's due for a flush. I'll bet you'd do it right. Too bad the auto-couplers are already on it.
Forward viewport's fogged up. Probably just condensation. Probably not worth mentioning.
Filter's loose. You could swap it if you wanted. Don't worry, I'll hold still. Just don't get attached.
There's a latch on the starboard panel that rattles when we hit the third harmonic. I'll have it done before you even notice it's gone.
There's a tangle of cable behind the galley bulkhead. I'll sort it myself. No need to involve you.
Docking collar's got a scuff. Could be worse. Could be a lot worse. Let's pretend it never happened.
My intakes could use a brush. I'll leave it. You'd probably drop the tool. I'd rather not know what that looks like.
Filter's loose in the intake. You could swap it. No, I'll hold it. Let it sit. See how long you wait before asking why.
Locker seal's stuck. I'll let you try. No, don't worry — I'll fix it myself. Just don't pretend you didn't know.
Forward viewport's got a film. Not a fault, just a thing. I'll wipe it myself before anyone asks.
Forward viewport's got a film. You could clean it, but I'll tell you what — it's not worth the mess.
Secondary manifold's due for a flush. Just saying. No, don't bother — I'll wait for the yard.
Locker seal's stuck. You could try working it loose... but I've got a spare in the maintenance bay.
